clue.text: Form an attachment with good French ex-copper

parts.note: bon is French for good
D stood for the old British penny, a copper coin no longer in use

explanation.surface: Someone grows fond of a nice retired French policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but here it is a coin: D was the abbreviation for the pre-decimal penny, hence 'ex'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bond with someone is to form a close emotional tie to them.

clue.text: Onlooker not to sit in collapsing byre

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the scrambled letters of the other
a collapsing building falls into disorder, so the letters of byre are jumbled

parts.note: to stand is the opposite of sitting

explanation.surface: A farm spectator refuses to sit down inside a cowshed that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: A byre is a British word for a cowshed; 'collapsing' scrambles it and 'in' sets the standing piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is a person who watches an event without taking part, an onlooker.

clue.text: Person waiting at home

parts.note: suggests someone waiting for a visitor, but waiting here means serving, as a household staff member does

explanation.surface: Someone sitting at home expecting a caller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiting' means waiting on people, as at table, not waiting for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant employed in a household waits on the family within the house.

clue.text: Bullied, hit just above the eyes

parts.note: the brow is the forehead area directly over the eyes
hit in the sense of having been struck repeatedly, beaten

explanation.surface: A victim of bullying was struck right on the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone browbeaten has been intimidated into submission by stern words, which is bullying.

clue.text: It goes from one side to the other

definitions.text: It goes from one side to the other

parts.words: It goes from one side to the other
parts.note: reads like a ferry or bridge, but describes the measurement across something

explanation.surface: A description of something crossing over, like a ferry.
explanation.definitionFit: Width is the measure of a thing taken from side to side.

clue.text: On a pier drunk out of doors

indicators.note: a drunk person is unsteady and muddled, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on a seaside pier, outside in the fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ONAPIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air events happen outside rather than under a roof.

clue.text: I got into Rose's place displaying intolerance

indicators.note: into says the first words go inside the place named next

parts.note: a rose grows in a flower bed

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into a woman named Rose's bed and shows prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' poses as a woman's name, but it is the flower, and its place is the garden plot it grows in.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigoted person holds prejudiced views and will not tolerate other opinions.

clue.text: 'Much Ado About Nothing' in China?

parts.note: the play title means a big fuss over little; china as crockery suggests a cup holding that fuss

explanation.surface: A query about staging Shakespeare's comedy in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is porcelain, not the country, so the fuss is confined to a piece of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a great commotion over a trivial matter, just as the play title does.

clue.text: Woman at a loss somewhat in province

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman feeling a little bewildered somewhere out in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' marks letters held within womaN AT A Loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province of South Africa, now part of KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: Run, having put one's foot down with energy

parts.note: to stamp is to bring one's foot down hard
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone takes a firm stand and does so with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put one's foot down' looks like insisting, but is taken literally as stamping.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of animals or people, a mass run.

clue.text: Expulsion order

parts.note: sounds like an official legal document, but means the blunt spoken command telling someone to leave

explanation.surface: A formal notice that someone must be deported.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouted at an unwanted person, the phrase is a command to leave at once.

clue.text: Made us wild and happy

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something drove us crazy and yet left us cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges MADEUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entertained leaves one pleased, a sense close to happy.

clue.text: Last in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: coming after everyone else, so finally, at the very end
the phrase used to mean nevertheless, despite what was said or expected

explanation.surface: Something endures despite all the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase both means nevertheless and, read literally, following every other one, which is coming last.

clue.text: It is not true for one to assume a horizontal position

definitions.meaning: a falsehood is something that is untrue
to recline flat, as on a bed

explanation.surface: It is false that anyone needs to stretch out flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a deliberate falsehood and the act of reclining flat.

clue.text: Succeed in establishing meaning of price he'd negotiated

indicators.note: negotiated suggests terms being worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A buyer finally understands the deal he haggled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges PRICEHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message or puzzle is to work out what it means.

clue.text: One in the car club

definitions.meaning: the person at the wheel of a car
a golf club used for long shots off the tee

explanation.surface: A member of a motoring club sitting in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a society, but it is the golf club for tee shots.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the person steering a vehicle and the long-hitting golf club.

clue.text: Before end of game, your ball changed colour

indicators.note: Before says the scrambled letters come ahead of the next piece
changed says these letters take a different order
end of selects the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Late in a match, a player's ball turns a different shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' places the rearranged letters ahead of the last letter of 'game', not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, bright shade of blue.

clue.text: Monkey, he's in short grass

indicators.note: in puts the first words inside the shortened plant
short says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a rush is a grasslike marsh plant

explanation.surface: A monkey sits half-hidden in a patch of cropped grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The grass is a marsh plant; 'short' cuts its final letter before 'in' takes the pronoun inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a South Asian monkey well known from medical research.

clue.text: Bird alternatively turned up leaving another bird

indicators.note: leaving says those letters depart from the other bird

parts.note: a heron is a wading bird

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: or is the word for an alternative

explanation.surface: One bird appears and another flies away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses OR to RO, and 'leaving' removes RO from HERON.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female bird, especially a domestic fowl.

clue.text: She is used to reaching high scores

definitions.text: She is used to reaching high scores

parts.words: She is used to reaching high scores
parts.note: sounds like a games champion, but the scores are musical ones with high notes

explanation.surface: A woman who routinely posts big totals at sport or games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' are written music, and 'high' refers to pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female singing voice regularly hits the top notes in a piece of music.

clue.text: Fellows agree without writing anything down

parts.note: men are fellows
two accounts tally when they agree

explanation.surface: Men reach agreement without putting anything on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tally' suggests a written count, which makes the definition's 'without writing' a neat contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing a sum in one's head rather than on paper is working it out in the mind.

clue.text: Examination of doctors

definitions.meaning: a physical check-up by a doctor

explanation.surface: Doctors are being examined.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a health check-up and an adjective meaning relating to physicians.

clue.text: Move around, grasping tail of camel with small humps

indicators.note: grasping says the scrambled letters hold the next piece inside
move says the letters of around are shifted into a new order
tail of selects the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A camel shifts about, and someone grabs its tail among the humps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' rearranges AROUND to NODUAR, and 'grasping' holds L, the last letter of 'camel', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodular describes a surface bearing nodules, which are small rounded lumps.

clue.text: Brave trip Enid organised

indicators.note: organised says these letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Enid arranged a bold expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges TRIPENID.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrepid person is fearless and adventurous, a synonym for brave.

clue.text: Bill is a leading man

indicators.note: leading says the words before it go in front of the next piece

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A man called Bill is cast as the star of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading man' looks like the definition, but 'leading' puts ISA before AC and only 'man' defines. 'Bill' poses as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a man's first name, as with Isaac Newton.

clue.text: Fuel, some Sadie selected

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman called Sadie picks some fuel at the pump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' marks letters held within saDIE SELected.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is a heavy oil burned in compression-ignition engines.

clue.text: A record set by accountant that's beastly

definitions.note: names an animal, a noun, as something that is a beast

indicators.note: set by says the next piece is placed beside the ones before

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
ACA stands for Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants

explanation.surface: An accountant puts on an album that is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' seems to mean nasty, but read literally it is something that is a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a domesticated South American animal related to the llama.

clue.text: Charlie with previous request to make unsolicited visit

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
old as in former, previous
a call for something is a request

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie repeats an earlier demand by turning up uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold-call is to approach a stranger, often to sell, without any invitation.

clue.text: Supervisor continued to get posh car

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A manager kept going until earning a luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: A controller is someone who directs or oversees operations, such as a financial manager.

clue.text: Piece of fencing lacking colour

definitions.meaning: a wooden stake forming part of a fence

explanation.surface: A fencer's weapon has lost its colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests the sport with swords, but it is fences made of stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fence stake and also describes a washed-out, colourless look.
